title: SRM School of Law Hosts 8th National Tamil Moot Court Competition with All-Women Final Bench
summary: Government Law College, Dharmapuri, won SRM School of Law's 8th National Level Tamil Moot Court Competition, whose final round was judged by an all-women panel.
body_html:
Chennai, 27 October 2026: SRM School of Law, SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST), Kattankulathur, hosted the 8th National Level Tamil Moot Court Competition 2026, bringing together 42 teams and 126 participants from law institutions across India. The final round was adjudicated by an all-women panel of five distinguished legal professionals, placing women's leadership and equal opportunity in the legal profession at the centre of the event.

Government Law College, Dharmapuri, won the competition, and Mother Teresa Law College finished as runner-up. The Best Memorial and Best Researcher awards went to participants from Government Law College, Karaikudi, while the Best Speaker award was presented to a participant from Government Law College, Tirunelveli.

The final-round panel comprised Hon'ble Justice (Retd.) Prabha Sridevan, former Judge of the Madras High Court; Professor Dr. N. Kayalvizhi, Principal, Dr. Ambedkar Government Law College, Pattaraiperumbudur; Professor Dr. Jaya Gowri, Principal, Dr. Ambedkar Government Law College, Pudupakkam; Senior Advocate Geetha of the Madras High Court; and Senior Advocate G. V. Shobha of the Madras High Court. The panel spoke about the importance of women's representation in law and the role educational institutions can play in building a more inclusive legal community. The organisers linked this focus to United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5 on gender equality.

The competition ran in three stages. In the preliminary rounds, 42 judges assessed teams on how they interpreted and applied the law, used legal authorities, reasoned through their cases and answered questions from the Bench. Eight teams reached the quarterfinals, a knockout stage that tested persuasive argument, courtroom etiquette and the ability to defend a legal position under scrutiny.

The event also promoted Tamil as a language of courtroom advocacy, giving law students from across the country a platform to argue complex legal questions in Tamil and build confidence in the courtroom, and highlighting the value of making legal education more accessible.

Addressing the participants, Hon'ble Justice Bhavani Subbarayan (Retd.) stressed the importance of strong research, drafting, pleading and analytical skills, along with practical exposure and a firm commitment to justice. Hon'ble Justice N. Mala of the Madras High Court encouraged students to accept both success and failure as part of their professional journeys, describing failure as a stepping stone to success. Speaking as a first-generation lawyer, she shared how she overcame self-doubt and urged students to uphold integrity and keep learning throughout their careers.

SRM School of Law said the competition reaffirmed its commitment to experiential legal education, linguistic inclusivity and gender equality, bringing together students, judges, senior members of the Bar and academic leaders on one platform.
